content:
The test image shows soybean pods that are heavily browned, shriveled, with what appears to be cottony white mycelial growth between them. The stem also shows lesions. Top candidates: **White_Mold** (cottony mycelium on pods), **Phomopsis** (pod blight/browning), **Anthracnose** (dark pod lesions).

Let me view one White Mold reference to confirm.

The White Mold reference shows bleached/straw-colored stems and wilted pods — that doesn't match well. The test image shows dark orange-brown to dark brown shriveled pods with pod decay and stem spotting.

Key observations from test image:
- Affected part: **pods** (and stem)
- Color: orange-brown to dark brown, severely shriveled/decayed pods
- Some fuzzy texture visible (pod hairs, possibly some mycelium)
- Stem has dark irregular spots/lesions
- Pods appear deflated/collapsed

This pattern — pod blight with brownish pod discoloration, shriveling, and stem lesions — is most consistent with **Phomopsis** (Phomopsis longicolla), which causes pod and stem blight with characteristic brown pod rotting. White Mold showed a bleached appearance, not matching the darker browns here.
